lines: <pulse>Back</pulse> to shelving before someone comes looking for a book I moved.
I should return to the catalog before my notes stop making sense.
There are loose pages waiting for thread and a steady hand.
The back shelves will not sort themselves, however firmly I wish otherwise.
I have three village records to finish before supper.
I need the quiet of my desk for a while.
A damaged binding has been waiting patiently enough.
I should get back before the ink dries in the wrong place.
Someone filed a farming ledger with the travel journals. I need to fix that.
The library needs me more than this conversation does now.
I left a book open, and that is bothering me more by the moment.
There is a stack beside the lectern leaning toward disaster.
I promised to find an old map before nightfall.
Time for me to count what came back and what did not.
I have a villager waiting for an answer I have not found yet.
The shelves are quiet, which usually means somebody moved something.
I should put today in writing while the details are still clear.
Enough talking for now. My work is starting to glare at me.
I need to mend a cover before one tear becomes five.
Come find me later. I will be where the paper and arguments gather.
